threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep waiting for the bus on Mare Street, but you’ve never figured out that it stops at the traffic lights, not the shelter.
Last Friday, I saw a guy on the 45 singing opera – had the whole bus in stitches. Gotta love the late-night vibes in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I watched my neighbor argue with a pigeon over the last piece of bread in front of the bakery. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a techno party happening in a former public toilet. Talk about creative reuse!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can name the taco truck that’s parked at 16th and Valencia but can’t tell you the BART schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo all dressed up, but he was on the Muni with a pizza box. Only in San Francisco, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals are night owls, but I swear, it's the early morning bakeries that reveal the real Gràcia vibe—quiet yet buzzing with life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle to decipher the 'hora punta' signs at the metro stations—total deer in headlights.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'the tube' like it's an actual person—'I'll take the tube' instead of just saying the Overground. Classic rookie mistake.
Caught a night bus last week, and the driver had to mediate a row between two mates over who owed for the kebab. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I spotted a flock of parrots sunbathing on the roof of a kebab shop. It's the little things that make you feel at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find currywurst served with a side of techno beats at a street vendor late at night—pure Berlin chaos and delight.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by whether they know to avoid 16th & Mission during BART delays—it's an urban battlefield out there.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full business attire get up from a Muni seat to help a lost tourist with a map—only in SF would you see that kind of kindness in rush hour chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the real charm is in the narrow streets where locals sip vermut on a sunlit afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they order a 'café con leche' and don’t know it's just coffee with milk. Locals take their coffee black or with a shot of espresso.
